longboat-key.summary: Longboat Key is a 10-mile barrier island between Sarasota Bay and the Gulf of Mexico, and one of Florida's quietest luxury resort communities. The island is overwhelmingly residential, favoring low-rise condominiums and Gulf-front and bayfront homes over commercial development, and beach access is the main event: miles of soft, uncrowded sand define daily life, kept serene in part by deliberately limited public parking and very little retail. At its heart, The Resort at Longboat Key Club anchors island life with 45 holes of championship golf (the Gulf-side Islandside course and the bayfront Harbourside layouts) alongside the deep-water Longboat Key Club Moorings, a 291-slip marina that berths vessels up to 150 feet. The 2024 arrival of The St. Regis Longboat Key Resort, set on 18 beachfront acres with 800 feet of private Gulf frontage, has further sharpened the island's standing among discerning buyers. The result is a market defined by privacy, water, and a slower, more residential rhythm than anywhere else on the Sarasota coast.

siesta-key.summary: Siesta Key is an eight-mile barrier island off Sarasota, reached by two bridges and built around a beach that is repeatedly ranked among the best in the country. The sand is the reason: it is almost pure quartz, ground fine over millions of years, and it stays cool underfoot in August when nothing else in Florida does. Three public beaches divide the island. Siesta Beach anchors the north end with the pavilion, the courts and the crowds; Crescent Beach runs south of it in a quieter arc; and Turtle Beach, at the far south end, trades white sand for a coarser shell mix, deeper water close in, and the island's only campground. Point of Rocks, the limestone outcrop at the south end of Crescent, is where the snorkeling is. Residentially the island reads in three layers. The Gulf front is condominium territory, much of it built between the 1960s and the 1980s and held tightly by owners who have been here for decades. Behind it sit the canal-front single-family homes, most with a dock and Intracoastal access. Siesta Key Village on the north end keeps the whole thing walkable, low-rise and deliberately unpolished, which is a large part of why people who buy here stop looking anywhere else.
